verdicts.evidence: references/complexity-signals.md:3-4 — "The signal names, model axis, and effort axis that every plan-producing skill/agent emits and every gate/executor consumes." The claim's own counter-quote (planner.md:516-517, "are what `gate-plan-review` and `sprint-execution` use to validate or select model/effort; emit them honestly rather than deriving model/effort first and back-filling signals to match") does not say "do not declare" — it forbids back-filling signals to a pre-chosen tier, a different rule. Residual note for the owner, which is a different finding than the one claimed: the planner declares at lines 36-37 that it owns `## Parallel Execution Map`, but no file in dev-kit-core defines that section's format — `grep -rn "Execution Map"` returns only consumers (gate-plan-review.md:34/52 scoring its `Model`/`Effort` columns, sprint-execution/SKILL.md:39/118) plus writing-plans/SKILL.md:86 deferring to the planner, and the planner's own PLAN.md template (lines 415-494) omits the section entirely. (verified verbatim; the agent's only dependency-graph rendering, and it is inline ASCII). `grep -rn -i "diagram\|mermaid" agents/planner.md references/planning/ references/vertical-slice.md references/complexity-signals.md references/summary-template.md references/thinking-models/planning.md skills/writing-plans/` returns zero hits — the absence itself is verified.
verdicts.reasoning: The factual half survives: nothing in the planner or its chain names the `diagram` skill, and the KICKOFF sentence must be KEPT. But the classification does not. `unenforced-gap` is defined as the guide asserting behavior the skill fails to enforce *of its own* — the planner nowhere claims to render a dependency diagram, and its plan format has no slot for one, so it is not failing its own contract; no downstream consumer requires a rendered graph either (`grep -rn "Execution Map"` shows gate-plan-review and sprint-execution read Model/Effort columns and `complexity:` blocks, not a diagram). Naming a second skill to invoke alongside the agent is textbook operator tool-wiring, which the rubric puts squarely on the load-bearing side ("which other artifact to feed in", "mode selection"). Refuted as a skill defect; keep the text as a load-bearing parameter, low severity.
